input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds Customer (Meridian) with an undefined, worldwide non-compete covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition of any competing product or service, extending 24 months post-term. That exceeds both the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer) and the walk-away threshold (post-term non-compete over 12 months / undefined "competes with Vendor" scope). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion; a narrowed fallback (named product, term only, ≤12 months, carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions) is offered in the comment.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or businesses we may build, buy, or sell, so we have deleted the 24-month worldwide non-compete in § 12.4, which also directly contradicts the freedom-to-operate confirmation in § 12.3. If Copperleaf needs protection for a specific offering, we can discuss a narrow restriction limited to one named competing product, during the term only and no more than 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
